feat(albanese): prove Milne Lemma 3.3 -- indeterminacy into a group variety is empty or pure codim 1

The indeterminacy locus Z(f) of a rational map f : X -> G from a nonsingular
variety to a group variety over k-bar is empty or of pure codimension one:
every point of Z(f) lies in the closure of a coheight-1 point OF Z(f).

Route (component reduction): fix x in Z(f); take a Noetherian affine window
W containing x; let C be the irreducible component of x in Z(f) cap W;
Jacobson-select an ambient-closed x0 in C avoiding the other components; the
Hauptidealsatz transport at x0 yields z in Z(f) with z specializing to x0 and
coheight z = 1; the closure of z lies in a component, which must be C since
x0 avoids the others, so C's generic point zeta generises z; zeta in Z(f) is
not the generic point of X (that one is in dom f), so coheight zeta >= 1, and
coheight strictness along zeta -> z forces zeta = z. Hence x in C = closure
{z}.

This was the last open obligation of the codim-one extension chapter and the
highest-leverage node of the cone (22 unlocks / 23 uses on the blueprint
frontier). Consequences:

  * Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean is now sorry-free.
  * extend_to_av (Milne Theorem 3.2: a rational map from a nonsingular
    variety to an abelian variety extends uniquely to a regular morphism) is
    UNCONDITIONAL, and axiom-clean: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
    only, verified with #print axioms.

The proof and its eight substep layers (CMEquidim, KernelGen, TransportLocal,
Rows, Diagonal, RowSection, Pullback, Transport) are ported from the sibling
Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild tree, which had developed them
sorry-free on the identical toolchain and mathlib pin. Every algebra
prerequisite already existed in this tree (AuslanderBuchsbaum, CoheightBridge,
SmoothPrimeRegularity, StandardSmoothDimension), so the port retargets
imports onto those hosts; zero declaration-name collisions.

Milne 3.3 lands in the new Albanese/Milne33.lean rather than in
CodimOneExtension.lean because its substep layers import the latter -- stating
it there would be an import cycle. It is split into a proof core carrying the
IrreducibleSpace / scheme-separated binders the argument uses directly, plus a
consumer-facing wrapper whose binder set matches the rest of the Milne I.3
chain and which derives those two instances. CodimOneExtension's stale
'single remaining sorry' status prose is corrected to point at the proof, and
isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth (Stacks 00TT) is made non-private so the
transport layer can consume it.

feat(albanese): the g-fold sum C^g -> A and its S_g-symmetry (Milne's 'clearly this is symmetric')

Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property (III.6 Prop 6.1) opens with
'clearly this is symmetric, and so it factors through C^(g)', where 'this' is

  C^g -> A,  (P_1, ..., P_g) |-> phi(P_1) + ... + phi(P_g)

for phi : C -> A into an abelian variety. This supplies that morphism and the
content behind the word 'clearly'.

  * powSum n phi : (prod_{i : Fin n} C) -> A, the product over i of the
    projections composed with phi.
  * permAut C sigma, the factor-permuting automorphism of C^n.
  * powSum_perm : permAut C sigma >> powSum n phi = powSum n phi -- the
    S_n-symmetry, which is exactly the hypothesis that the universal property
    of Sym^n C consumes.
  * comp_powSum, naturality in the source.

THE MECHANISM, because it makes the geometry evaporate. Mathlib's
CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Mon.lean already equips the hom-set (X -> A)
of a monoid object in a cartesian monoidal category with a Monoid structure
whose multiplication is DEFINITIONALLY lift f h >> mu[A], and upgrades it to a
CommMonoid when A is a commutative monoid object. Over (Spec kbar) is cartesian
monoidal and braided, and an abelian variety is a commutative group object
there. So the g-fold sum is a Finset.prod of morphisms and its symmetry is
Equiv.prod_comp. Stating it this way is not a shortcut: it is the observation
that Milne's 'clearly' is the commutativity of A's group law and nothing else.

One piece Mathlib was missing: it gives the hom-set its monoid structure but
never records that PRECOMPOSITION respects it. Added as MonObj.preHom, a
MonoidHom (X -> A) ->* (W -> A) (multiplicativity is comp_lift, unitality is
uniqueness of the map to the unit object). That is what lets map_prod move a
precomposition through the finite product, and it is reusable beyond this file.

Axiom-clean: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

SCOPE, stated so nobody mistakes this for more than it is. This does NOT
construct Sym^g C. At this Mathlib pin there is no quotient of a scheme by a
finite group action, and the project's own analogies/m3-route-audit.md scopes
that construction at ~2400-3800 LOC (action typeclass, affine quotient
Spec R^G with its universal property, the glued global quotient, and
smoothness of Sym^n C for a curve). What lands here is the INPUT to the
symmetric power's universal property -- the half of Milne's symmetrisation
step that does not depend on the quotient existing.

Milne, Abelian Varieties, III.6 Prop 6.1, p. 104; blueprint
lem:symmetric_product_av_map.

feat(albanese): descent from a dense open into an abelian variety -- the extension half of Milne III.6.1's psi

Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property reaches "it therefore defines a
rational map psi : J -> A, which (I 3.2) shows to be a regular map". This lands
that sentence in the form the descent actually needs, with no rational map in the
statement:

  exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open :
    given a DENSE OPEN V of a nonsingular kbar-variety X and ANY morphism
    h : V -> A into an abelian variety, compatible with the structure maps,
    there is a UNIQUE g : X -> A with V.iota >> g = h.

Existence is extend_to_av (Milne Thm 3.2), which became unconditional earlier in
this run when Milne Lemma 3.3 closed. Uniqueness is the reduced-and-separated
agreement principle. Axiom-clean: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

The enabling lemma, and the reason the statement can avoid rational maps at all:

  hom_toRationalMap_eq_partialMap_iff :
    g.toRationalMap = (PartialMap.mk V hV h).toRationalMap  <->  V.iota >> g = h

A Scheme.RationalMap is a QUOTIENT of partial maps, so extend_to_av's conclusion
is an identity in that quotient, and every call site would otherwise have to
unfold it. This bridge discharges the quotient once, via
PartialMap.equiv_iff_of_isSeparated_of_le with the common dense open V. Also
extracted isSeparated_left_of_isProper (scheme-level separatedness of an AV from
properness of its structure map), which three declarations in the leg were
each proving inline.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE REMAINING GAP, stated precisely rather than
optimistically. It does NOT prove descentThroughBirationalSigma. What it does is
establish that the extension is no longer any part of the obstruction: the moment
one has a dense open of Pic^0 and a morphism from it to A, the unique global psi
and its defining equation follow with no further geometric input -- no
birationality, no properness of V, nothing about where h came from. So the
Albanese descent's remaining content is exactly (i) Sym^g C and f^{(g)} existing,
and (ii) Milne III Thm 5.1(a) birationality in a usable form, i.e. a SECTION of
f^{(g)} over a dense open. Mathlib at this pin has no birational-inverse API
(Birational/{RationalMap,Dominant}.lean supply IsDominant, not an inverse), so
(ii) is a real construction, not a lookup.

descentThroughBirationalSigma's docstring is updated to name this lemma and to
state the residual gap in those two pieces.

Milne, Abelian Varieties, I.3 Thm 3.2 and III.6 Prop 6.1 p. 104; blueprint
lem:descent_through_birational_sigma.

64: \begin{definition}[Indeterminacy locus of a rational map]\leanok

69:   % (read from references/abelian-varieties.pdf, PDF page 22).
70:   % SOURCE QUOTE: "A rational map \(\varphi\) is said to be \emph{defined} at a point
71:   % \(v\) of \(V\) if \(v \in U\) for some \((U, \varphi_U) \in \varphi\). The set \(U_1\) of
72:   % \(v\) at which \(\varphi\) is defined is open, and there is a regular map
73:   % \(\varphi_1 \colon U_1 \to W\) such that \((U_1, \varphi_1) \in \varphi\) --- clearly,
74:   % \(U_1 = \bigcup_{(U, \varphi_U) \in \varphi} U\) and we can define \(\varphi_1\) to be
75:   % the regular map such that \(\varphi_1 | U = \varphi_U\) for all $(U, \varphi_U) \in
76:   % \varphi$."
77:   \textit{Source: Milne, \emph{Abelian Varieties}, \S I.3, p.~16.}
78:   Let \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y\) be a rational map between varieties over \(\bar k\).
79:   The \emph{domain of definition} of \(f\) is the open set
80:   \[
81:     \mathrm{Dom}(f) \;:=\; \bigcup_{(U, \varphi_U) \in f} U \;\subseteq\; X,
82:   \]
83:   i.e.\ the union of the dense opens of all representatives of \(f\). The
84:   \emph{indeterminacy locus} of \(f\) is the closed complement
85:   \[
86:     Z(f) \;:=\; X \smallsetminus \mathrm{Dom}(f) \;\subseteq\; X.
87:   \]
88:   The map \(f\) is regular (i.e.\ defined on all of \(X\)) if and only if \(Z(f) = \emptyset\).
89: \end{definition}

91: \begin{lemma}
92: [Indeterminacy locus is closed]
93:   \label{lem:isClosed_indeterminacy_locus}
94:   \uses{def:indeterminacy_locus}
95:   For any rational map \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y\) of schemes, the
96:   indeterminacy locus \(Z(f) = X \smallsetminus \mathrm{Dom}(f)\)
97:   (\cref{def:indeterminacy_locus}) is a closed subset of \(X\): it is the
98:   complement of the open domain of definition \(\mathrm{Dom}(f)\).
99: \end{lemma}

101: \begin{proof}
102:   The domain of definition is open, and the complement of an open subset is closed.
103: \end{proof}

    11	
    12	Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property (*Abelian Varieties* III.6
    13	Proposition 6.1) reaches the point "it therefore defines a rational map
    14	`ψ : J ⇢ A`, which (I 3.2) shows to be a regular map". This file supplies that
    15	sentence in the form the Albanese descent actually needs.
    16	
    17	## The statement
    18	
    19	`extend_to_av` (Milne Theorem 3.2, `Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`)
    20	extends a `Scheme.RationalMap` into an abelian variety to a unique morphism.
    21	But a `RationalMap` is a *quotient* of partial maps, so applying it and then
    22	identifying the result requires unfolding that quotient at every call site.
    23	
    24	`exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open` states the same content in
    25	elementary terms:
    26	
    27	> given a **dense open** `V ⊆ X` and *any* morphism `h : V ⟶ A` into an abelian
    28	> variety which is compatible with the structure maps over `k̄`, there is a
    29	> **unique** morphism `g : X ⟶ A` with `V.ι ≫ g = h`.
    30	
    31	No rational maps appear in the statement. That is the form a descent step wants:
    32	one produces a morphism on the locus where things are defined, and reads back a
    33	morphism on all of `X` together with the equation identifying it there.
    34	
    35	## Why this is the right shape for the Albanese descent
    36	
    37	Milne's `ψ` is built by inverting the birational `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰` on
    38	the dense open where it is an isomorphism, and composing with `Sym^g φ`.
    39	Mathlib at this pin has **no** API for inverting a birational morphism (see
    40	`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Birational/{RationalMap,Dominant}.lean`: there is
    41	`IsDominant` machinery but no inverse-on-a-dense-open construction). So the
    42	`Pic⁰ ⇢ A` rational map cannot yet be produced.
    43	
    44	What this file establishes is that *producing it is the only remaining gap*: the
    45	moment one has a dense open `V ⊆ Pic⁰` and a morphism `V ⟶ A` (e.g. a
    46	section of `f^{(g)}` over `V` followed by `Sym^g φ`), the unique global `ψ` and
    47	its defining equation follow with no further geometric input. The extension half
    48	of `descentThroughBirationalSigma` is therefore closed; the birationality half
    49	is what remains.
    50	
    51	## Main results
    52	
    53	* `Scheme.RationalMap.hom_toRationalMap_eq_partialMap_iff` — for a morphism
    54	  `g : X ⟶ A` into an abelian variety and a dense open `V`, the rational-map
    55	  identity `g.toRationalMap = (PartialMap.mk V hV h).toRationalMap` is equivalent
    56	  to the elementary equation `V.ι ≫ g = h`. The bridge that removes the quotient.
    57	* `Scheme.RationalMap.exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open` — the descent
    58	  statement above.

   117	structure morphisms over `k̄`. Then there is a **unique** morphism `g : X ⟶ A`
